english.html: newcomer certain things among the most hidden, on which neither the one nor the other had yet been interrogated, nor on anything that came near them; which was done, and truly (as was since verified) answered by him. Afterwards, having had him withdrawn, they have the prisoner brought in, to whom they put the same interrogations, up to the number of ten or twelve, who answers in everything like the other. Which astonished the company, and made them fall into the opinion that the prisoner had something of magic — as indeed he was ill-famed for it in the said places of Artigat, Le Pin, Sagias and other neighbouring places.

There was certainly great reason to think that this accused had some familiar spirit, seeing that he knew so well and truly how to answer of all things, even the most secret and private, without ever failing by a nail's breadth. And (what is far more to be wondered at) he knew all those who presented themselves to him, at the beginning and afterwards, without ever having seen them. Which could not fall within instructions or memoranda that had been given him by another; and particularly since he had never (that anyone knew) been at the place of Artigat, nor conversed with the inhabitants of that place. cachees, & deſquelles ny l'vn ny l'autre
n'euſt eſté encor interrogué, ni de choſe
qui en approchaſt. ce que fut fait, & par
luy veritablement (comme depuis fut ve-
rifié) reſpondu. Apres l'ayant fait tirer,
font venir le priſonnier, auquel font les
meſmes, & iuſqu'au nombre de dix ou
douze interrogatoires, qui reſpond en
tout comme l'autre. Ce que fit esbahir
la compagnie, & tomber en opinion, que
le priſonnier euſt quelque choſe de la
magie: comme auſſi il en eſtoit diffamé
eſdits lieux d'Artigat, du Pin, de Sagias,
& autres circonuoiſins.
Il y auoit certes grande raiſon, de penſer que ce pre-
uenu euſt quelque eſprit familier, veu qu'il ſçauoit ſi
bien & veritablement reſpondre de toutes choſes, meſ-
mement des plus ſecrettes, & priuees, ſans iamais fail-
lir d'vn trauers d'ongle. Et (qui eſt bien plus à admi-
rer) cognoiſſoit tous ceux qui ſe preſenterent à luy
du commencement, & apres ſans les auoir veuz onc-
ques. Ce que ne pouuoit tomber en inſtructiõs, ni me-
moires qui luy euſſent eſté baillées par autre: & ſingu-
lierement qu'il n'auoit iamais eſté au lieu d'Artigat
(qu'on ſceut) ni conuerſé auec les habitans de ce lieu.
Et ne faut douter qu'entre les prodigieuſes & abomi-
nables tyrannies, que Satan depuis la creation du mon
de a cruellement exercees contre les hommes, pour les
enlacer & attirer à ſon regne, il n'ayt tenu vn grãd ma-
